subject: geography
topicDisplay: The Changing Landscapes Of The UK
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A delta forms where a river:
options: Deposits its load as it enters a sea or lake
Begins at its source on a mountain
questions.explain: Deltas form where a river deposits sediment as it slows on entering still water.

questions.q: Mass movement at the coast, such as a landslide or slumping, occurs when:
options: Sediment is carried out to sea by waves
Material moves down a cliff under gravity, often after rain saturates it
questions.explain: Mass movement is the downhill movement of cliff material under gravity, often triggered by water saturation.

questions.q: A waterfall and its plunge pool are typically formed where the river crosses:
options: A band of soft rock over hard rock
A band of hard rock over softer rock
questions.explain: Soft rock beneath a hard cap is eroded faster, forming a waterfall and plunge pool.

questions.q: Which best explains why longshore drift moves sediment in a zig-zag?
options: Swash comes in at an angle but backwash drains straight down the beach
questions.explain: Wind-driven swash arrives at an angle while gravity pulls backwash straight down, moving sediment in a zig-zag.

questions.q: Which of these is HARD engineering coastal defence?
questions.explain: A sea wall is a hard engineering structure that reflects wave energy.

questions.q: The coastal erosion process where waves throw pebbles against a cliff, wearing it away, is:
questions.explain: Abrasion occurs as waves hurl sediment against the cliff, grinding it away.

questions.q: A disadvantage of using groynes as a coastal defence is that they:
options: Starve beaches further along the coast of sediment, increasing erosion there
questions.explain: By trapping sediment, groynes deprive beaches downdrift, which can erode more quickly.

questions.q: The boundary separating one drainage basin from another is the:
questions.explain: The watershed is the ridge of high land marking the edge of a drainage basin.

questions.q: Transport in which small particles bounce along the river bed is called:
questions.explain: Saltation is the bouncing or hopping of small particles along the bed.

questions.q: Constructive waves are best described as:
options: High, frequent waves with a strong backwash that erode beaches
Low, gentle waves with a strong swash that build up beaches
Waves that flow inland as rivers
Waves that only occur in storms
questions.explain: Constructive waves have a strong swash and weak backwash, depositing material to build beaches.

questions.q: Beach nourishment is an example of:
questions.explain: Beach nourishment, adding sand or shingle, is a soft engineering approach.

questions.q: In the water cycle, water soaking down into the soil is called:
questions.explain: Infiltration is the movement of water from the surface down into the soil.

questions.q: Solution (corrosion) as a coastal erosion process involves:
options: Weak acids in seawater dissolving rocks such as limestone
questions.explain: Solution is the chemical dissolving of soluble rocks like chalk and limestone by slightly acidic seawater.

questions.q: Destructive waves:
options: Have a strong backwash that removes material and erodes the coast
questions.explain: Destructive waves have a strong backwash and steep, frequent form, eroding the coast.

questions.q: A salt marsh often develops behind a spit because:
options: The sheltered water allows fine sediment and mud to be deposited
questions.explain: Sheltered, calm water behind a spit lets mud and silt settle, creating a salt marsh.

questions.q: Large boulders piled at the base of a cliff to absorb wave energy are called:
questions.explain: Rock armour is large boulders placed at the cliff foot to absorb and break wave energy.

questions.q: When a spit grows across a bay, joining two headlands and trapping a lagoon behind it, it forms a:
questions.explain: A bar forms where a spit extends across a bay, often enclosing a lagoon.

questions.q: Which is a HUMAN cause of increased river flooding?
options: Building on floodplains and creating impermeable surfaces
questions.explain: Urbanisation adds impermeable surfaces and drains, speeding water into rivers.

questions.q: Vertical erosion in a river's upper course tends to create which valley shape?
questions.explain: In the upper course the river cuts down vertically, forming a steep V-shaped valley.

questions.q: The process by which water turns from liquid into vapour and rises into the atmosphere is:
questions.explain: Evaporation turns liquid water into water vapour that rises into the air.

questions.q: The change in direction at the end of a spit, forming a curved hook, is mainly caused by:
options: A change in the coastline shape or a second wind/wave direction
questions.explain: A secondary wind or wave direction, or a bend in the coast, curves the end of a spit into a recurved hook.

questions.q: The area of land drained by a river and its tributaries is the:
questions.explain: A drainage basin is the whole area of land drained by a river system.
